title: Combined migrator powers (unstakeFor + onlyOwnerOrMigrator on withdrawRewardToken) yield a single-key drain of all NFTs and all phUSD
description:
Looked at individually each migrator power is a documented (or at least implementable) administrative control. Looked together they constitute the complete economic surface of the staker. The migrator can:
  1. Call `unstakeFor(beneficiary_i, users[beneficiary_i].amount)` for each known beneficiary, in any order, until totalStaked == 0. NFTs land at the migrator (line 558); each beneficiary's pending phUSD is paid to them at this stage.
  2. With totalStaked == 0, cooperate with pauser (or be pauser) to call `pause()`.
  3. Call `withdrawRewardToken(migratorAddr, fullBalance)` to drain the remaining phUSD.

After the sequence: migrator holds every id-6 NFT that was deposited via stakeFor/stake, AND the residual phUSD reward budget (everything that wasn't paid out as in-flight pending during step 1). Beneficiaries hold only the pending phUSD that accrued up to their respective unstakeFor moment — which can be near zero if the migrator runs the sequence immediately after a topup or recompute.

The plan does not document this combined capability. The plan models the migrator as a stateless helper that orchestrates one direction (deposit) of one migration. The implementation gives the same role the ability to undo every deposit AND sweep the reward pool. The aggregate value at stake is the full staker TVL: all migrated id-6 NFTs + the runway-matching phUSD mint.
impact: If the migrator role is ever assigned to a non-stateless or non-trusted address (whether by mistake, future-incident re-assignment, or contract bug), the entire staker can be drained in a single transaction sequence executed by that address — no owner cooperation required for step 1, and owner cooperation needed only for step 2 if the migrator isn't also pauser. Magnitude: full staker TVL (~139 NFTs × spot price + funded runway). Constraint: requires the migrator role to be set to the eventual extractor. The plan assigns migrator = MigrationHelper, a stateless contract — so under the plan's deployment, this attack is structurally impossible. The finding is the unintended-privilege gap between plan and code: the contract authorises a much wider set of actions than the plan's helper actually uses, so any deviation from the planned helper expands risk dramatically.
recommendation: Apply the recommendations from ECON-01, ECON-02, and ECON-03 together: remove the migrator path from `withdrawRewardToken` (revert to plan-spec `onlyOwner`), remove or repurpose `unstakeFor` (it is not in the plan and creates the principal-redirection vector), and document the migrator's intended trust model explicitly on-chain. With those three changes, the migrator's only power is the documented `stakeFor` — which itself doesn't transfer beneficiary funds out of the staker. Trust surface collapses back to what the plan describes.
attack_scenario:
1. Owner deploys NFTStakerV2, funds runway with R phUSD (per plan step 11), sets targetAPY = 0.3e18.
2. Owner sets migrator = X (where X is intended to be MigrationHelper).
3. Users migrate; over time N id-6 NFTs accumulate in the staker.
4. At some point — could be the same deployment (owner mistake) or a future re-assignment (owner intentionally changes migrator for a follow-up incident, but the new migrator is bugged/compromised) — X is an address with the powers above. Sequence:
   a. For each known beneficiary B_i (enumerable from Staked/StakedFor events): `X.unstakeFor(B_i, users[B_i].amount)`. NFTs aggregate at X. Each B_i's pending phUSD at that moment is paid to B_i (correct routing per code), but the bulk of the reward budget is NOT yet paid out — only the small accrued slice since the last recompute for each user.
   b. After all unstakes, totalStaked == 0. Pause via X or via cooperative pauser.
   c. `X.withdrawRewardToken(X, rewardToken.balanceOf(staker))`. All phUSD lands at X.
5. End state: X holds all id-6 NFTs and the unaccrued portion of the phUSD budget. Honest beneficiaries hold only the small pending paid during step (a).

This is not exploitable by an outsider — only by whoever the owner sets `migrator` to. The finding's value is to flag that the owner's `setMigrator` call is a one-key authorisation of the entire staker economy, which the plan did not contemplate.
